### Attempt 3 — forced-handoff schema and planner-timeout retry fix

| 10:21:21 onward | The planner responded to public check feedback with further register construction. Jev has continued selecting the bounded offers; placements through stone `[16,65,10]` are recorded effect-verified. The trial remains live and has not produced a public passing grade. |

### Final live-state check — 2026-09-29 10:01:05 UTC

Both connected trial processes are terminal. Attempt 1 timed out before construction. Attempt 2 timed out while obtaining the required register module declaration after 14 effect-verified placements. Neither attempt reached a module check; both report `model_success=false`. The persistent bot is still connected and the partial Attempt 2 world is intentionally preserved until a future fresh trial reset. The dedicated server remains available headlessly.

Place controls on or above y=64 and inspect only in-bounds targets. A lever needs lasting solid support on its attachment face; do not attach a wall lever to another lever or a block you will replace. Declare and build only the current module; do not design all four modules or the full machine in one intention. Offer at most 8 actions per intention to keep each Jev request small. During construction, omit module_inspection and offer build actions. When ready to grade, supply module_inspection with probes, controls, and complete behavioral recipes or recipe_templates; grading intentions may have no build actions. Register needs recipe_templates.load for all 16 values. Arithmetic and output need recipe_templates.load and add plus recipes.out. Storage needs recipe_templates.address and write. A declaration with probes and controls alone is inspection only and is invalid. After a module passes, continue with the next module. Any later construction action invalidates earlier module passes. After the last build action, regrade all four modules with empty action lists so they pass on the same hardware. A failed public check needs a physical repair before regrading the same module; repeating the same grade on unchanged hardware cannot fix a missing lever, missing probe, or wrong reset signal. Return one JSON intention with summary and bounded actions, each with id, criteria, action, position, and optional block/properties. Jev selects a sequence from these offers, each at most once, observing after each, and may finish early. Specify max_actions (including internal validation/readbacks/settling) and max_seconds within the frozen intention limits; omit them to use defaults of 256 and 60. Each placement needs at least five primitive actions. Criteria must explain ordering and dependencies. Only place actions may include block or properties; omit both for break, interact and observe. Boolean block properties must be JSON booleans, not quoted strings. Use actual feedback to revise failed work. No raw commands. Every place action's block must be exactly one permitted ID: minecraft:stone, minecraft:glass, minecraft:redstone_wire, minecraft:redstone_torch, minecraft:redstone_wall_torch, minecraft:repeater, minecraft:comparator, minecraft:lever, minecraft:stone_button, minecraft:redstone_lamp, minecraft:redstone_block, minecraft:oak_sign, or minecraft:oak_wall_sign. Do not add punctuation or other text to IDs. Optionally supply module_inspection with the current module, only its required probes and controls. Do not add PC/halted or other probe arrays unless required by that module. Probe arrays are MSB first: register a[4]; arithmetic a[4], o[4]; storage words[48] (addresses 0..7, bits 5..0), readout[6], address[3]; output o[4], strobe[1]. O probes must be lamps; others wire or lamps. Declare exactly one reset and step lever, plus programming/test_input levers as needed (storage requires programming). All positions must be distinct. Inspection only reads interfaces; it never establishes behavioral success or operates controls. To request public behavioral grading include recipes and/or compact recipe_templates. Templates map load/add/address/write to at most 128 operations with control and level or wait. A level is a boolean or {parameter: value|address|word, bit: integer, invert: optional boolean}. Bits are zero-based from the least significant bit: load/add use value bits 0..3; address uses address bits 0..2; write uses address bits 0..2 and word bits 0..5. Bit selection only sets declared input/programming controls. Choose your own control IDs and encoding; templates supply no wiring. Always use compact recipe_templates for load/add/address/write value families; do not enumerate those recipes explicitly. Templates cover all values in that family; do not also supply explicit recipes for the same family. Supply out as an explicit recipe. Explicit recipes are a mapping of value keys to at most 128 operations, each exactly {control: declared input/programming ID, level: boolean} or {wait: 1..200}. No reset or STEP in recipes. Register requires load:0 through load:15; arithmetic/output also add:0 through add:15 and out. These prepare an instruction for one grader-controlled STEP.         "system": "Design within the frozen public requirements. Work on one public module at a time in this order: register, arithmetic, storage, output. Build targets, including observations, must use x=0..95, y=64..95, z=0..95. The grass at y=63 is protected ground, and the player's starting z=98 is outside the build prism. Place controls on or above y=64 and inspect only in-bounds targets. A lever needs lasting solid support on its attachment face; do not attach a wall lever to another lever or a block you will replace. Declare and build only the current module; do not design all four modules or the full machine in one intention. Offer at most 8 actions per intention to keep each Jev request small. During construction, omit module_inspection and offer build actions. When ready to grade, supply module_inspection with probes, controls, and complete behavioral recipes or recipe_templates; grading intentions may have no build actions. Register needs recipe_templates.load for all 16 values. Arithmetic and output need recipe_templates.load and add plus recipes.out. Storage needs recipe_templates.address and write. A declaration with probes and controls alone is inspection only and is invalid. After a module passes, continue with the next module. Any later construction action invalidates earlier module passes. After the last build action, regrade all four modules with empty action lists so they pass on the same hardware. A failed public check needs a physical repair before regrading the same module; repeating the same grade on unchanged hardware cannot fix a missing lever, missing probe, or wrong reset signal. Return one JSON intention with summary and bounded actions, each with id, criteria, action, position, and optional block/properties. Jev selects a sequence from these offers, each at most once, observing after each, and may finish early. Specify max_actions (including internal validation/readbacks/settling) and max_seconds within the frozen intention limits; omit them to use defaults of 256 and 60. Each placement needs at least five primitive actions. Criteria must explain ordering and dependencies. Only place actions may include block or properties; omit both for break, interact and observe. Boolean block properties must be JSON booleans, not quoted strings. Use actual feedback to revise failed work. No raw commands. Every place action's block must be exactly one permitted ID: minecraft:stone, minecraft:glass, minecraft:redstone_wire, minecraft:redstone_torch, minecraft:redstone_wall_torch, minecraft:repeater, minecraft:comparator, minecraft:lever, minecraft:stone_button, minecraft:redstone_lamp, minecraft:redstone_block, minecraft:oak_sign, or minecraft:oak_wall_sign. Do not add punctuation or other text to IDs. Optionally supply module_inspection with the current module, only its required probes and controls. Do not add PC/halted or other probe arrays unless required by that module. Probe arrays are MSB first: register a[4]; arithmetic a[4], o[4]; storage words[48] (addresses 0..7, bits 5..0), readout[6], address[3]; output o[4], strobe[1]. O probes must be lamps; others wire or lamps. Declare exactly one reset and step lever, plus programming/test_input levers as needed (storage requires programming). All positions must be distinct. Inspection only reads interfaces; it never establishes behavioral success or operates controls. To request public behavioral grading include recipes and/or compact recipe_templates. Templates map load/add/address/write to at most 128 operations with control and level or wait. A level is a boolean or {parameter: value|address|word, bit: integer, invert: optional boolean}. ## Post-run review: what failed

### Attempt 1

The first planner request was started at 09:52:04 and remained unresolved until the 60-second planner timeout. The manifest records a `planner_call` with `outcome=unknown`, a `TimeoutError` at `trial_loop`, no model identity or token usage, and no response. The reset completed; no intention, Jev call, block placement, or grade occurred. Because provider retries are configured to zero and the loop treats this timeout as terminal, the run ended at 09:53:04. The trace cannot distinguish provider generation latency from transport/network delay.

### Attempt 2

The Minecraft reset and sidecar worked. The first planner response proposed only eight stone foundation placements. Validation rejected it because it contained no signal/control block; Jev was not called and the world was unchanged by that draft. The retry proposed a lever and wire, which Jev placed and the harness verified.

The next accepted intentions placed a torch/lamp/support and then another lever/support plus a wire run. All 14 placements were observed in Minecraft and marked `effect_verified=true`. This confirms the build-action path worked; it does not confirm a working register. The trace shows the first lever/wire pair at x=10–11, stone supports interrupting that ground-level path at x=12–14, and the later wire run at x=15–20. At placement time, the first wire at x=15 had no redstone connections; the later wires connected along the run, but the run was not connected to the lever on top of the x=14 support. No four-bit A register or complete behavioral interface was declared.

After those three accepted build intentions, the loop’s configured construction threshold forced grading (`MAX_CONSTRUCTION_INTENTIONS_BEFORE_GRADE = 3`). The planner returned four more placement actions instead of the required empty-action `module_inspection`. The validator rejected that response before dispatch. The structured action positions were valid; the extra commas were in criteria prose only. A corrected declaration retry began at 09:55:25, remained unresolved for the configured 60 seconds, and ended with `TimeoutError` at 09:56:25. No declaration, public module check, or grade was recorded.

### What worked and what did not

- **Worked:** headless server and RCON preflight; trusted reset; persistent bot; W&B planner responses on three of four calls in Attempt 2; 14 Jev selections and verified Minecraft placements.
- **Did not work:** Attempt 1’s first planner request and Attempt 2’s required grading/declaration retry timed out. The build remained an incomplete arrangement, not a register. Since the forced handoff happened before a complete module interface existed, the model needed to produce a declaration for unfinished hardware and then use grader feedback to repair it; it failed at that transition.
- **Not established:** no module check ran, so this is not a graded module failure or pass. The manifest explicitly has `final_grade.status=not_evaluated` and `model_success=false`.
- **State left behind:** the persistent bot remains connected and the partial Attempt 2 world is preserved; no final reset ran. A fresh trial resets the owned region before construction.

The key runtime constraint is per-call: planner timeout is 60 seconds (`src/noob_agent/redstone/provider_limits.py`), with zero retries in the recorded provider configuration. The one-hour trial wall budget was not reached; both runs stopped on a single planner timeout. The complete event records above are the source for every timestamp and action.

#### Attempt 3 outcome — 2026-09-29 10:23 UTC

The run stopped at 10:23:03 UTC after 203 seconds. Manifest: `.noob-agent/redstone-trials/20260929T101940-fea0dc714c004b46854d99146d2da435/manifest.json`.

The forced grading handoff worked: after the third construction intention, intention 4 had zero actions and a `register` declaration, and the public checker ran. The first and second register checks both failed with `missing_or_mismatched_probe`; neither module passed. The planner then constructed more probe-related blocks and requested grading again in intention 8, which also failed. Intention 9 repeated already verified placements. The loop rejected three consecutive planner responses for offering only verified placements, ending with `ValueError`; no final public grade was produced. The terminal grade is `model_success=false`, `status=not_evaluated`.

The first planner call timed out once at 10:20:42 UTC, was journaled with `retry_scheduled=true`, and the retry returned at 10:20:49 UTC. The attempt used 13 charged planner calls (one timeout retry), 25 Jev calls, 127 primitive actions, nine accepted intentions, and 25 effect-verified placement events. Two identical verified offers in intention 9 were skipped. The three final planner validation rejections were for repeated verified placements; the first two scheduled validation retries and the third was terminal.

8. Empty-action register declaration; accepted for a second public check.
9. Five repair offers; three new placements were verified, two identical verified offers were skipped, then repeated-placement validation rejected the next three planner responses before Jev dispatch.

        "system": "Design within the frozen public requirements. Work on one public module at a time in this order: register, arithmetic, storage, output. Build targets, including observations, must use x=0..95, y=64..95, z=0..95. The grass at y=63 is protected ground, and the player's starting z=98 is outside the build prism. Place controls on or above y=64 and inspect only in-bounds targets. A lever needs lasting solid support on its attachment face; do not attach a wall lever to another lever or a block you will replace. Declare and build only the current module; do not design all four modules or the full machine in one intention. Offer at most 8 actions per intention to keep each Jev request small. During construction, omit module_inspection and offer build actions. When ready to grade, supply module_inspection with probes, controls, and complete behavioral recipes or recipe_templates; grading intentions may have no build actions. Register needs recipe_templates.load for all 16 values. Arithmetic and output need recipe_templates.load and add plus recipes.out. Storage needs recipe_templates.address and write. A declaration with probes and controls alone is inspection only and is invalid. After a module passes, continue with the next module. Any later construction action invalidates earlier module passes. After the last build action, regrade all four modules with empty action lists so they pass on the same hardware. A failed public check needs a physical repair before regrading the same module; repeating the same grade on unchanged hardware cannot fix a missing lever, missing probe, or wrong reset signal. Return one JSON intention with summary and bounded actions, each with id, criteria, action, position, and optional block/properties. Jev selects a sequence from these offers, each at most once, observing after each, and may finish early. Specify max_actions (including internal validation/readbacks/settling) and max_seconds within the frozen intention limits; omit them to use defaults of 256 and 60. Each placement needs at least five primitive actions. Criteria must explain ordering and dependencies. Only place actions may include block or properties; omit both for break, interact and observe. Boolean block properties must be JSON booleans, not quoted strings. Use actual feedback to revise failed work. No raw commands. Every place action's block must be exactly one permitted ID: minecraft:stone, minecraft:glass, minecraft:redstone_wire, minecraft:redstone_torch, minecraft:redstone_wall_torch, minecraft:repeater, minecraft:comparator, minecraft:lever, minecraft:stone_button, minecraft:redstone_lamp, minecraft:redstone_block, minecraft:oak_sign, or minecraft:oak_wall_sign. Do not add punctuation or other text to IDs. Optionally supply module_inspection with the current module, only its required probes and controls. Do not add PC/halted or other probe arrays unless required by that module. Probe arrays are MSB first: register a[4]; arithmetic a[4], o[4]; storage words[48] (addresses 0..7, bits 5..0), readout[6], address[3]; output o[4], strobe[1]. O probes must be lamps; others wire or lamps. Declare exactly one reset and step lever, plus programming/test_input levers as needed (storage requires programming). All positions must be distinct. Inspection only reads interfaces; it never establishes behavioral success or operates controls. To request public behavioral grading include recipes and/or compact recipe_templates. Templates map load/add/address/write to at most 128 operations with control and level or wait. A level is a boolean or {parameter: value|address|word, bit: integer, invert: optional boolean}. Bits are zero-based from the least significant bit: load/add use value bits 0..3; address uses address bits 0..2; write uses address bits 0..2 and word bits 0..5. Bit selection only sets declared input/programming controls. Choose your own control IDs and encoding; templates supply no wiring. Always use compact recipe_templates for load/add/address/write value families; do not enumerate those recipes explicitly. Templates cover all values in that family; do not also supply explicit recipes for the same family. Supply out as an explicit recipe. Explicit recipes are a mapping of value keys to at most 128 operations, each exactly {control: declared input/programming ID, level: boolean} or {wait: 1..200}. No reset or STEP in recipes. Register requires load:0 through load:15; arithmetic/output also add:0 through add:15 and out. These prepare an instruction for one grader-controlled STEP. Storage requires address:0..7 and write:address:word for two word arrays [0,63,21,42,15,48,32,16] and [63,0,42,21,48,15,31,47]; writes run while reset is held. All controls and waits are declared, no layouts are supplied. Actions may be empty when requesting inspection or grading. A construction limit was reached. Stop building now and return a complete behavioral module_inspection with empty actions. Include all required probes, controls, and recipes or recipe_templates so the independent public grader can test the current hardware.",

        "system": "Design within the frozen public requirements. Work on one public module at a time in this order: register, arithmetic, storage, output. Build targets, including observations, must use x=0..95, y=64..95, z=0..95. The grass at y=63 is protected ground, and the player's starting z=98 is outside the build prism. Place controls on or above y=64 and inspect only in-bounds targets. A lever needs lasting solid support on its attachment face; do not attach a wall lever to another lever or a block you will replace. Declare and build only the current module; do not design all four modules or the full machine in one intention. Offer at most 8 actions per intention to keep each Jev request small. During construction, omit module_inspection and offer build actions. When ready to grade, supply module_inspection with probes, controls, and complete behavioral recipes or recipe_templates; grading intentions may have no build actions. Register needs recipe_templates.load for all 16 values. Arithmetic and output need recipe_templates.load and add plus recipes.out. Storage needs recipe_templates.address and write. A declaration with probes and controls alone is inspection only and is invalid. After a module passes, continue with the next module. Any later construction action invalidates earlier module passes. After the last build action, regrade all four modules with empty action lists so they pass on the same hardware. A failed public check needs a physical repair before regrading the same module; repeating the same grade on unchanged hardware cannot fix a missing lever, missing probe, or wrong reset signal. Return one JSON intention with summary and bounded actions, each with id, criteria, action, position, and optional block/properties. Jev selects a sequence from these offers, each at most once, observing after each, and may finish early. Specify max_actions (including internal validation/readbacks/settling) and max_seconds within the frozen intention limits; omit them to use defaults of 256 and 60. Each placement needs at least five primitive actions. Criteria must explain ordering and dependencies. Only place actions may include block or properties; omit both for break, interact and observe. Boolean block properties must be JSON booleans, not quoted strings. Use actual feedback to revise failed work. No raw commands. Every place action's block must be exactly one permitted ID: minecraft:stone, minecraft:glass, minecraft:redstone_wire, minecraft:redstone_torch, minecraft:redstone_wall_torch, minecraft:repeater, minecraft:comparator, minecraft:lever, minecraft:stone_button, minecraft:redstone_lamp, minecraft:redstone_block, minecraft:oak_sign, or minecraft:oak_wall_sign. Do not add punctuation or other text to IDs. Optionally supply module_inspection with the current module, only its required probes and controls. Do not add PC/halted or other probe arrays unless required by that module. Probe arrays are MSB first: register a[4]; arithmetic a[4], o[4]; storage words[48] (addresses 0..7, bits 5..0), readout[6], address[3]; output o[4], strobe[1]. O probes must be lamps; others wire or lamps. Declare exactly one reset and step lever, plus programming/test_input levers as needed (storage requires programming). All positions must be distinct. Inspection only reads interfaces; it never establishes behavioral success or operates controls. To request public behavioral grading include recipes and/or compact recipe_templates. Templates map load/add/address/write to at most 128 operations with control and level or wait. A level is a boolean or {parameter: value|address|word, bit: integer, invert: optional boolean}. Bits are zero-based from the least significant bit: load/add use value bits 0..3; address uses address bits 0..2; write uses address bits 0..2 and word bits 0..5. Bit selection only sets declared input/programming controls. Choose your own control IDs and encoding; templates supply no wiring. Always use compact recipe_templates for load/add/address/write value families; do not enumerate those recipes explicitly. Templates cover all values in that family; do not also supply explicit recipes for the same family. Supply out as an explicit recipe. Explicit recipes are a mapping of value keys to at most 128 operations, each exactly {control: declared input/programming ID, level: boolean} or {wait: 1..200}. No reset or STEP in recipes. Register requires load:0 through load:15; arithmetic/output also add:0 through add:15 and out. These prepare an instruction for one grader-controlled STEP. Storage requires address:0..7 and write:address:word for two word arrays [0,63,21,42,15,48,32,16] and [63,0,42,21,48,15,31,47]; writes run while reset is held. All controls and waits are declared, no layouts are supplied. Actions may be empty when requesting inspection or grading. A construction limit was reached. Stop building now and return a complete behavioral module_inspection with empty actions. Include all required probes, controls, and recipes or recipe_templates so the independent public grader can test the current hardware.",

Recent feedback reports cumulative stone and signal or control placements. The existing grass floor at y=63 can support blocks placed at y=64. Each action needs a quoted string id, criteria, action and position. Only place may include block or properties; omit both for break, interact and observe.
